findings.title: Controller-level Customer policy prevents Staff from calling mature endpoint
findings.claim: DepositsController is annotated with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] at the class level, which ASP.NET Core applies conjunctively with the action-level [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Staff)] on the Mature endpoint. Consequently, Staff users who do not have the Customer role receive a 403 Forbidden response when attempting to mature deposits.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] from the DepositsController class declaration. The Open and Break endpoints already declare [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] on their respective actions.
findings.requirement_link: Maturing a deposit via POST api/deposits/{id}/mature (Policies.Staff) or IDepositService.MatureAsync performs no owner check and throws InvalidOperationException if the deposit is not Open or if clock.UtcNow < MaturesAt.

findings.title: Controller-level Customer policy blocks Staff access to Mature endpoint
findings.claim: In ASP.NET Core, [Authorize] attributes are evaluated additively across class and action levels. Because DepositsController is decorated with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)], the Mature action decorated with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Staff)] requires callers to satisfy both policies, returning HTTP 403 Forbidden to staff accounts and preventing staff execution.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] from the class declaration (or replace it with [Authorize] without policy), as Open, Mature, and Break already specify their respective Customer and Staff policies on each action method.
findings.requirement_link: Maturing a deposit via POST api/deposits/{id}/mature (Policies.Staff) or IDepositService.MatureAsync performs no owner check and throws InvalidOperationException if the deposit is not Open or if clock.UtcNow < MaturesAt.

findings.title: Controller-level Customer authorization policy blocks Staff from mature endpoint
findings.claim: In ASP.NET Core, authorization attributes combine additively. Because `[Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)]` is declared on DepositsController, the `Mature` action requires both `Policies.Customer` and `Policies.Staff`, which prevents pure Staff users from maturing deposits.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove `[Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)]` from the controller class level (or replace with bare `[Authorize]`), keeping explicit policy checks on individual actions (`Open` and `Break` already specify `Policies.Customer`).
findings.requirement_link: Maturing a deposit via POST api/deposits/{id}/mature (Policies.Staff) or IDepositService.MatureAsync performs no owner check and throws InvalidOperationException if the deposit is not Open or if clock.UtcNow < MaturesAt.

findings.title: Unbounded memory growth in DepositLocks ConcurrentDictionary
findings.claim: DepositLocks stores a SemaphoreSlim for each deposit ID processed in MatureAsync and BreakAsync but never removes entries. Over the lifetime of the application, this static collection will grow unbounded as term deposits are matured or broken.
findings.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, SemaphoreSlim> DepositLocks = new();
findings.suggested_fix: Clean up unused semaphores using TryRemove once the lock is released and no other threads are waiting, or use a size-bounded eviction cache.

findings.title: Unbounded memory accumulation in static DepositLocks dictionary
findings.claim: DepositLocks stores a SemaphoreSlim instance for every deposit ID passed to MatureAsync or BreakAsync without an eviction or cleanup mechanism. Because entries are added before confirming whether the deposit exists and are never pruned, this results in continuous memory growth over time and creates a potential resource exhaustion vector.
findings.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, SemaphoreSlim> DepositLocks = new();
findings.suggested_fix: Use keyed lock striping or a size-bounded/sliding cache with eviction, or rely on database-level row locking / concurrency tokens rather than an unbounded static dictionary.

findings.title: Static DepositLocks dictionary leaks memory over time
findings.claim: DepositService allocates a SemaphoreSlim for each deposit ID into a static ConcurrentDictionary that is never pruned. Every deposit that is matured or broken leaves an entry in memory indefinitely, causing unbounded resource consumption over the application's lifetime.
findings.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, SemaphoreSlim> DepositLocks = new();
findings.suggested_fix: Rely on database transaction concurrency control (such as concurrency tokens or row versioning) rather than an unbounded in-memory static dictionary, or evict lock entries once transitions complete.
findings.requirement_link: Double-payout or race condition: concurrent MatureAsync and BreakAsync calls (or repeated calls) on the same Open deposit could pay out principal or interest twice if state transitions and persistence are not strictly guarded.

findings.title: No test coverage for non-EUR multi-currency deposit lifecycle
findings.claim: All test fixtures hardcode EUR accounts and verify ledger balances only in EUR. The requirement highlights multi-currency ledger routing to DepositHolding and InterestExpense as an operational risk, but non-EUR flows are unexercised.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test scenario creating and maturing a deposit with a non-EUR account (such as USD) to verify multi-currency holding and expense account routing.
findings.requirement_link: OpenAsync derives CustomerId from ICurrentUser.UserId and Currency from the source account, transfers principal from accountId to BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.DepositHolding, currency) via ILedger.PostTransferAsync

findings.title: Staff-only maturity enforcement required by acceptance criteria is not tested
findings.claim: The acceptance criteria mandate automated xUnit tests verifying Staff-only maturity enforcement. Existing tests only invoke IDepositService.MatureAsync directly using a caller that still has the Customer role, without asserting that non-Staff callers are rejected.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an integration or controller test verifying that POST api/deposits/{id}/mature permits Staff callers and returns Forbid or Unauthorized for Customer callers.
findings.requirement_link: Automated xUnit tests verify: 3/6/12-month rate mapping and interest rounding half away from zero, principal < 500 and invalid term rejection, owner enforcement on open and break, Staff-only maturity enforcement, rejection of premature maturity, rejection of breaking or maturing an already closed deposit, and ledger balances across Customer, DepositHolding, and InterestExpense accounts.
